elements.label: Elevator doors sliding shut from both sides, covering the woman standing inside

sfx_review.label: unsure
sfx_review.note: About 0.2 s before this shot starts (belongs to the e018 button press); broadband transient, no sweep, so not clearly a whoosh.

sfx_review.label: impact
sfx_review.note: Broadband onset lands as the doors meet and the frame settles on the closed doors; reads as a soft door-close thud or music hit rather than a chime. Medium confidence.

pattern.description: Live-action elevator doors slide in from both edges and meet in the centre, closing over the subject so the doors themselves act as a two-sided wipe that ends on a clean, neutral frame.
pattern.why_premium: An in-world object performs the transition, so the cut to the next scene is motivated by the story; the converging doors also land on a beat and leave a calm empty frame to cut from.

build_hint.gsap: Recreate as a split mask wipe: two panels tl.fromTo(leftDoor, {xPercent: -100}, {xPercent: 0, duration: 0.38, ease: 'power2.inOut'}) and tl.fromTo(rightDoor, {xPercent: 100}, {xPercent: 0, duration: 0.38, ease: 'power2.inOut'}, '<'), the scene behind static; land the meet on the audio hit.
build_hint.remotion: Two absolutely positioned door panels with translateX = interpolate(frame, [0, 10], [-100, 0], {easing: Easing.inOut(Easing.quad), extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) percent (mirrored for the right); no spring, doors meet without overshoot.

notes: Live-action footage; camera verdict none. Only the doors move; the woman is static and gets covered. Pattern could alternatively be treated as a mask_wipe transition into the next shot.
